prayerExcerpt.en-US: This is my body which will be given for you; do this as a memorial of me
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Isto é o meu corpo, que é dado por vós; fazei isto em memória de mim.

meta.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle; his eyes lifted in thanksgiving. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle. St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle. The other Apostles behind, each different: St. Andrew as on the andrew card, an old man with curly grey-white hair and a long grey-white beard forked in two points; St. James the Greater as on the james_greater card, a young man of about twenty-eight with chestnut hair to the jaw and a sparse short beard; St. Thomas as on the thomas_apostle card, a beardless young man of about twenty-five with short dark hair; St. Bartholomew as on the bartholomew card, a man of about forty-five with black curly hair and a long black beard beginning to grey.
meta.basis: The Institution of the Eucharist at the Last Supper (Lk 22:19-20; Mk 14:22-24) with John leaning on the Lord's breast (Jn 13:23), painted at the moment of the blessing of the bread rather than the betrayal, as Juan de Juanes did. Christ, Peter and John from recurring-figures.md; the other Apostles from their cards.
